question.prompt: Points \(D,\) \(E,\) \(F\) are taken respectively on sides \(AB,\) \(BC,\) and \(CA\) of triangle \(ABC\) so that \(AD:DB=1:n,\) \(BE:CE=1:n,\) and \(CF:FA=1:n.\) The ratio of the area of triangle \(DEF\) to that of triangle \(ABC\) is:

solutions.explanation:
The three corner triangles are easier to compare with \(ABC\) than the central triangle is. For the stated positive side ratios, \(n>0\), so \(n+1>0\). Let \([XYZ]\) denote the area of triangle \(XYZ\).

The ratios give \(AD/AB=1/(n+1)\) and \(AF/AC=n/(n+1)\). Triangles \(ADF\) and \(ABF\) have bases on the same line \(AB\) and share the altitude from \(F\), so
\[
\frac{[ADF]}{[ABF]}=\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac1{n+1}.
\]
Triangles \(ABF\) and \(ABC\), using bases \(AF\) and \(AC\), share the altitude from \(B\). Hence
\[
\frac{[ABF]}{[ABC]}=\frac{AF}{AC}=\frac n{n+1}.
\]
Multiplying these ratios gives
\[
\frac{[ADF]}{[ABC]}=\frac n{(n+1)^2}.
\]
At corner \(B\), the adjacent side fractions are \(BD/BA=n/(n+1)\) and \(BE/BC=1/(n+1)\). At corner \(C\), they are \(CE/CB=n/(n+1)\) and \(CF/CA=1/(n+1)\). The same common-altitude argument therefore gives this same area fraction for \(BDE\) and \(CEF\).

These three corner triangles and \(DEF\) partition \(ABC\), with no overlapping interiors. Thus
\[
\frac{[DEF]}{[ABC]}
=1-\frac{3n}{(n+1)^2}
=\frac{n^2-n+1}{(n+1)^2},
\]
which is choice A.
solutions.title: Remove the three corner triangles
